Denuvo has won court approval to subpoena Discord, Valve and Reddit in an attempt to identify the anonymous game cracker known as “voices38.”

Denuvo originally asked for a huge amount of information, including payment records, transaction history, login logs and posts/comments. But the judge raised privacy concerns and said the requests went way beyond what was needed to identify the person.

Denuvo then cut the requests down. The new subpoenas mainly ask for information that could reveal voices38’s identity, such as their name, email address, IP addresses, phone number and physical address.

Fallout: New Vegas just got a huge visual upgrade thanks to a new RTX Remix mod from Kim2091.

The New Vegas RTX project is now playable in a work-in-progress state, bringing full path tracing to the Mojave.

The mod adds:

- Full path-traced lighting and reflections with realistic light bouncing and softer shadows
- Path-traced sun, moon, fires, neon signs, and muzzle flashes
- Path-traced Pip-Boy flashlight
- A physically based sky with clouds, atmosphere, stars, and moon
- Path-traced water with waves, reflections, and caustics
- Support for DLSS, FSR, and XeSS
- NVIDIA Reflex and DLSS Ray Reconstruction/Frame Generation support

Despite the RTX name, the mod isn’t limited to NVIDIA hardware; the creator says it also works with AMD RX 6000+ and desktop Intel Arc GPUs.

Lucasfilm Games is becoming more flexible about who gets to make Star Wars games.

After Star Wars: Zero Company and Star Wars: Galactic Racer, Lucasfilm Games executive Douglas Reilly says the company is now more open to pitches from different developers and publishers.

“We’re more flexible about, like, who we’re willing to take pitches from and good ideas can come from a lot of different places.”

The change comes after EA’s 10-year exclusivity deal ended in 2023, opening the door for more studios to work on Star Wars.

“You don’t have to necessarily be a top five publisher to make a great Star Wars game.”

But the company is clearly willing to look beyond the biggest names in the industry. Reilly says Lucasfilm is exploring projects with “large and small partners” that could “continue to surprise folks.”

Halo Studios reportedly worked on a Halo game that mixed battle royale and extraction shooter mechanics before the project was scrapped.

The game, known internally as Project Ekur, apparently evolved from Project Tatanka, an earlier battle royale project connected to Halo Infinite.

According to a report from HiddenXperia, Ekur would have had players dropping onto Zeta Halo, with the playable area gradually shrinking. Players could play as either a UNSC Spartan or, for the first time, a Banished Brute.

The map would also feature AI-controlled Flood enemies that could infect areas of the map, while players fought rival squads and potentially teamed up to take down large bosses.

The Flood storyline was intended to connect the game to a future Halo 7.

Ekur was eventually abandoned as more developers were moved to help with Campaign Evolved.
